title: Seven-month-old with a cough and fast breathing

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Hello, come on in. So this is Arlo? And you're mum and dad?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Yes, I'm Hannah and this is Callum.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Hello both. What's been happening with Arlo?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: He's had a runny nose and a cough for four days, and since yesterday his breathing's gone really fast.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: How old is he now?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Seven months.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Has he had a temperature?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: A little bit. 37.9 this morning.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: How's he feeding? Is he on bottles?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Bottles, yes. He's taking most of his bottles, I'd say.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Hannah, he isn't. He's only managed about half of each bottle since yesterday. I did the night feeds.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Oh. Yes, that's true, he keeps pulling off to breathe.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Okay, so about half his usual amount since yesterday. How many wet nappies has he had in the last 24 hours?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Four, I think. He'd usually have six or seven.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Has he had any pauses in his breathing, where he stops breathing for a few seconds?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: No. His sister did, though, when she had bronchiolitis two years ago. She stopped breathing in the night and we had to call an ambulance. That's why we're so scared.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: That must have been frightening. So none of that with Arlo?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: No, nothing like that with him.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Has he gone blue or very pale at all?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any vomiting or diarrhoea?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: He brought up a bit of milk after coughing, that's all.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Was he born on time, and any problems since birth?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Born at 39 weeks, no problems.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any heart or lung problems?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Is he up to date with his vaccinations?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Yes, all of them.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any medicines or allergies?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Just Calpol once yesterday. No allergies.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Does anyone at home smoke?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: I do, but only outside, never in the house.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Thanks, Callum. Let me examine Arlo. His temperature is 37.8. He's breathing about 54 times a minute. His heart rate is 150. His oxygen level is 95 percent. I can see he's pulling in a little under his ribs when he breathes, so a bit of extra effort. His capillary refill is under two seconds. He's alert and looking around.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Is that bad?

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Let me listen. I can hear crackles and some wheeze on both sides of his chest. This all fits with bronchiolitis, a common virus in babies.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Does he need to go to hospital?

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: He's working a bit harder to breathe, and his feeding is down to about half, which is right on the line. His oxygen is okay and he's alert. I think it's reasonable to look after him at home for now, but I want to see him again tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Give him smaller feeds more often. You can use saline drops in his nose before feeds to help clear it. Bronchiolitis often gets worse over the first three to five days before it gets better.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: If he has any pauses in his breathing, goes blue, or is really struggling to breathe, call 999.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: If he's taking less than half his usual feeds, has no wet nappy for 12 hours, or seems more tired and floppy, call us or 111 straight away, even overnight.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: We will. Thank you.

reference_note.presenting_complaint: Cough and coryza for 4 days, increased work of breathing since yesterday.
reference_note.history: Coryza and cough for 4 days; fast breathing since yesterday. Temperature up to 37.9 °C. Feeding about half his usual amount since yesterday (initially reported by mother as most feeds; father, who did night feeds, confirmed about half). Four wet nappies in 24 hours (usually 6–7). No apnoeas (older sister had an apnoea with bronchiolitis two years ago). No cyanosis. Small posset after coughing. Born at 39 weeks, no neonatal problems. No cardiac or respiratory history. Immunisations up to date. Father smokes (outdoors only).
reference_note.medications_allergies: Paracetamol once yesterday. No known drug allergies.
reference_note.examination: Temperature 37.8 °C. RR 54, HR 150, SpO2 95% in air. Mild subcostal recession. CRT under 2 seconds. Alert. Bilateral fine crackles and wheeze.
reference_note.impression: Bronchiolitis with moderately reduced feeding; borderline for referral (feeds about 50%). Managed at home with early review.
reference_note.plan: Small, frequent feeds; saline nose drops before feeds. Advised illness may worsen over days 3–5. Clinical review tomorrow morning.
reference_note.safety_netting: Call 999 if pauses in breathing, blue colour, or severe difficulty breathing. Call GP or 111 urgently if feeds fall below half, no wet nappy for 12 hours, or more tired or floppy.
